feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: seasonal ET dynamics can be simulated well with single-column ELM across representative sites in the Passaic basin, but rigorous validation is constrained because there are no long-term AmeriFlux/eddy-covariance towers located inside the Passaic River basin itself. The nearest suitable flux tower (US-Slt, Silas Little, NJ Pine Barrens) lies ~100 km south in a different physiographic/land-cover setting.
answerable: Seasonal (monthly/DJF-MAM-JJA-SON) ET magnitude and phasing at representative Passaic-basin points
Partitioning of ET into transpiration, ground/soil evaporation, and canopy evaporation
Sensitivity of ET seasonality to land cover (forest vs. developed vs. wetland) and soil texture
Comparison of simulated latent/sensible heat fluxes against out-of-basin NJ flux towers (US-Slt) as a plausibility/benchmark check
not_answerable: Point-for-point in-basin eddy-covariance validation (no in-basin long-term flux tower exists)
Spatially distributed/routed basin-integrated ET (single-column ELM has no lateral hydrology or river routing)
Sub-daily ET closure diagnostics matched to a specific tower footprint within the basin

parsed.n_justification: Four columns span the dominant land-cover/soil gradients controlling ET in the Passaic basin: (1) upland deciduous forest in the northern Highlands headwaters, (2) suburban/developed lowland near the main-stem valley, (3) the Great Swamp wetland complex (a key ET hotspot), and (4) a benchmark column co-located with the US-Slt Silas Little flux tower to enable eddy-covariance comparison. This captures the primary controls on seasonal ET while keeping the ensemble small and interpretable.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) forcing at four lat/lon points
Surface dataset generation (mksurfdata) with site-appropriate PFT/soil overrides
Monthly and daily history output streams (h0/h1)
AmeriFlux US-Slt Level-2/BASE eddy-covariance data for benchmark comparison
assumptions: Satellite/NLCD-informed PFT assignment: deciduous broadleaf forest (highlands), mixed low-veg/developed (lowland), wetland/graminoid (Great Swamp), needleleaf/oak-pine (US-Slt)
A 200-year accelerated-decomposition + regular spinup precedes the 2000-2014 transient run to equilibrate soil moisture and C/N pools
GSWP3 forcing at ~0.5deg is downscaled/applied per point; local microclimate biases (urban heat, wetland saturation) are only partially represented
Validation is treated as benchmarking against US-Slt rather than in-basin validation due to absence of in-basin flux towers
Single-column mode ignores lateral groundwater flow and streamflow routing; wetland column ET may be underestimated without a saturated-zone override
SP (satellite-phenology) mode may be substituted for BGC if only biophysical ET seasonality (not carbon coupling) is required
